Skip next section Unknown Christmas work by Humperdinck discovered 09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 Unknown Christmas work by Humperdinck discovered Timothy Jones Humperdinck's best-known work is the opera 'Hansel and Gretel' Image: dpa A "Christmas Lullaby" by composer Engelbert Humperdinck (1854-1921) donated by his great-grandson to his birth city of Siegburg has been confirmed to be a previously unknown work. "For the music world, the find is a sensation," city spokesman Jan Gerull told the DPA news agency. The one-page manuscript with the work for four-voice male choir was given to the Siegburg city archive by Humperdinck's great-grandson, Lothar Witte, some time ago for its collection related to the composer. Humperdinck is Siegburg's best-known son Image: Fine Art Images/Heritage Images/IMAGO The head of the Musicwerkstatt Siegburg, Christian Ubber, said it had first had to be clarified whether Humperdinck had used and published the work in another context. "This examination took some time and turned out negative so that it is only now certain that this 'Christmas Lullaby' was really unknown up to now," he said. According to city spokesman Gerull, the piece, a highly indivualized version of the German Christmas song "Josef lieber, Josef mein," is not easy to sing owing to the composer's sometimes complex style. But, he said, this had not dampened the enthusiasm. "Siegburg is looking forward to having the piece performed before Christmas," he said. https://p.dw.com/p/5NWKt Skip next section Cabinet gives green light to care system reform package 09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 Cabinet gives green light to care system reform package Timothy Jones The German Cabinet has put its seal of approval on a draft bill put forward by Health Minister Carsten Linnemann on reforming the care system. The proposed reforms, which will now be put before the parliament, seek to prevent an estimated shortfall of some €8-10 million ($9 to $11 million) next year. The reforms were the subject of heated debate between the conservative bloc of Christian Democrats (CDU), to which Linnemann belongs, and its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU), and the junior coalition party the Social Democrats (SPD). The draft bill builds largely on proposals by former Health Minister Nina Warken, also from the CDU. No details on the exact content of the bill as it now stands have been released. https://p.dw.com/p/5NVgX Skip next section Bundeswehr failing to tackle sexual harassment — report 09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 Bundeswehr failing to tackle sexual harassment — report Timothy Jones Many women in the Bundeswehr have been victims of sexual offenses Image: Marcus Brandt/dpa/picture alliance The German armed forces are doing too little to crack down on instances of sexual offenses against women in their ranks, according to public service broadcaster ARD. This comes as the Bundeswehr is actively seeking to recruit women. Witnesses and victims of such offenses told the ARD's news magazine REPORT MAINZ that many personnel were scared to report what had happened to them for fear of negative career consequences. The number of suspected cases of sexual harassment has been rising every year, with 413 reported in 2024 and 472 in 2025, but the number of unreported cases is likely high, according to the ARD. A spokeswoman from the Defense Ministry told REPORT MAINZ that there had been an "disproportionate rise" in reports of sexual offenses this year. Women have been permitted to join the Bundeswehr in all capacities for 25 years but still make up just 13.6% of personnel. The Defense Ministry has, however, rejected the claim by a military historian in the program that the integration of women in the Bundeswehr had so far failed. Women in the Bundeswehr were "accepted and respected," and there was no "value and rights free space for any group of people" in the German armed forces, it said. https://p.dw.com/p/5NVvg Skip next section Cabinet debates care reform after uncertainty 09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 Cabinet debates care reform after uncertainty Timothy Jones The German Cabinet is to discuss the draft bill put forward by Health Minister Carsten Linnemann to reform the care system after much heated debate between the coalition partners, the Federal Press Office in Berlin has said. Duisburg police said the officers would execute a number of arrest warrants and confiscate up to €48.6 million ($55.15 million) of illicit funds. More than 100 locations were to be searched, with 71 people under investigation. Searches are being carried out in the states of North Rhine-Westphalia , Rhineland-Palatinate , Baden-Württemberg , Berlin and Bavaria , as well as in Belgium , Bulgaria and the Netherlands . According to police, those under investigation are suspected of "forming a criminal association, predatory and commercial blackmail, gang and commercial fraud and commercial money-laundering." They are also believed to be behind weapons offenses, physical assault and tax avoidance. The operation is under the supervision of state prosecutors in Duisburg, with the involvement of the State Office for Combating Financial Criminality in North Rhine-Westphalia (LBF). https://p.dw.com/p/5NV9Q Skip next section Coalition in race to put care reform debate to rest 09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 Coalition in race to put care reform debate to rest A package of reforms to Germany's care system put forward by conservative Health Minister Carsten Linnemann remains a source of contention within the coalition. It remained unclear early on Wednesday whether a planned morning Cabinet meeting to agree on the package called by Linnemann would take place. The junior coalition partner, the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) , opposes any cuts to care services. Among other things, it has called for a cap on personal contributions to care in retirement homes and financial adjustments to make the division fairer between private and statutory nursing care insurance models. Both ideas have met with skepticism from Linnemann. The reform of the system has been made necessary by the growing number of people needing care as the population ages, which has raised costs.
